\chapter{Work and Marriage}
\label{ch:hi-work-and-marriage}
\hlchaptermodality{119}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask and answer about a job, a profession, a wedding, being married, and a birthday.}

Complete HI-C119-janmdin: the questions that come after a name.

\section[naukrī]{\hi{नौकरी} (naukrī) — a job}

\label{lesson:HI-C119-naukri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a wife, then the Hindi for a relative.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{नौकरी}}
\textbf{\hi{नौकरी}} (\emph{naukrī}) — \textquotedblleft{}a job\textquotedblright{}, employment.

\textbf{\hi{आपकी} \hi{नौकरी} \hi{कहाँ} \hi{है}?} — \textquotedblleft{}where is your job?\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}where do you work?\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The second question after a name.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naukrī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naukrī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{āpkī naukrī kahā̃ hai?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a wife, then the Hindi for a relative, then say \emph{naukrī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{नौकरी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A job\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[peśā]{\hi{पेशा} (peśā) — a profession}

\label{lesson:HI-C119-pesha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a relative, then the Hindi for a job.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पेशा}}
\textbf{\hi{पेशा}} (\emph{peśā}) — \textquotedblleft{}a profession\textquotedblright{}, a trade.

\textbf{\hi{नौकरी}} is the job you hold; \textbf{\hi{पेशा}} is what you are by trade. \textbf{\hi{आपका} \hi{पेशा} \hi{क्या} \hi{है}?}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A job, and the profession behind it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peśā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peśā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{āpkā peśā kyā hai?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a relative, then the Hindi for a job, then say \emph{peśā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{पेशा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A profession\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[śādīśudā]{\hi{शादीशुदा} (śādīśudā) — married}

\label{lesson:HI-C119-shadishuda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a profession, then the Hindi for a wedding.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{शादीशुदा}}
\textbf{\hi{शादीशुदा}} (\emph{śādīśudā}) — \textquotedblleft{}married\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\hi{शादी}} with \textbf{-\hi{शुदा}}, \textquotedblleft{}having been done\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\hi{क्या} \hi{आप} \hi{शादीशुदा} \hi{हैं}?} — \textquotedblleft{}are you married?\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A question you will be asked early and often.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{kyā āp śādīśudā haiṁ?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a profession, then the Hindi for a wedding, then say \emph{śādīśudā} again

\section[janmdin]{\hi{जन्मदिन} (janmdin) — a birthday}

\label{lesson:HI-C119-janmdin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a wedding, then the Hindi for married.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{जन्मदिन}}
\textbf{\hi{जन्मदिन}} (\emph{janmdin}) — \textquotedblleft{}a birthday\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}birth-day\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{दिन}} is the day you know. \textbf{\hi{जन्मदिन} \hi{की} \hi{शुभकामनाएँ}} — \textquotedblleft{}happy birthday\textquotedblright{}, with the good wishes you have.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A job, a profession, a wedding, married, a birthday.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{janmdin}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{janmdin}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{janmdin kī śubhkāmnāẽ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a wedding, then the Hindi for married, then say \emph{janmdin} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
